svg.text: Algorithm 3 — Fast column algorithm (exhaustive reduction in O(n^ω) time)

text.tspan: Augment: R = [D 0; 0 I] (16 × 16), V = I. The columns [1, 8] are processed by a binary recursion; whenever a column
turns out to be zero it is swapped with a column of I, so the first k processed columns always hold k pivots.
Node [1, 8]: split into B = [1, 4] (green) and C = [5, 8] (gray). Recurse on B first;
afterwards all pivots found in B are applied to C in one batch.
Node [1, 4]: split into B = [1, 2] (green) and C = [3, 4] (gray). Recurse on B first;
afterwards all pivots found in B are applied to C in one batch.
Leaf 1: column 1 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(1) = 5 is its pivot.
Apply B = [1] to C = [2]: pivot row L = ⟨5⟩ (green).
R[L, C] = 0, so Λ = 0 and nothing changes.
Leaf 2: column 2 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(2) = 2 is its pivot.
Apply B = [1, 2] to C = [3, 4]: pivot rows L = ⟨5, 2⟩ (green), one per column of B.
Permute the rows L to the bottom, in the same order as the columns of B.
After the permutation R[L, B] (orange outline) is lower triangular with non-zero diagonal (Lemma 4.3), hence
invertible in O(k^ω) with k = 2. R[L, C] (dashed) is the block to be zeroed; orange columns are the ones Λ will change.
Schur complement: Λ ← R[L, B]⁻¹ · R[L, C]; R[L̄, C] ← R[L̄, C] − R[L̄, B] · Λ; R[L, C] ← 0. Arrows: each non-zero Λ[t, c]
applies pivot column t (green) to column c (orange). One 2×2 inversion and one (n×2)(2×2) product do it all at once.
Result (dark gray = updated entries): the pivot rows are zero in C.
Undo the row permutation (implicit index bookkeeping in practice, Lemma 3.2).
Recurse on C = [3, 4].
Leaf 3: column 3 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(3) = 8 is its pivot.
Apply B = [3] to C = [4]: pivot row L = ⟨8⟩ (green).
R[L, C] = 0, so Λ = 0 and nothing changes.
Leaf 4: column 4 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(4) = 4 is its pivot.
Apply B = [1, 4] to C = [5, 8]: pivot rows L = ⟨5, 2, 8, 4⟩ (green), one per column of B.
Permute the rows L to the bottom, in the same order as the columns of B.
After the permutation R[L, B] (orange outline) is lower triangular with non-zero diagonal (Lemma 4.3), hence
invertible in O(k^ω) with k = 4. R[L, C] (dashed) is the block to be zeroed; orange columns are the ones Λ will change.
Schur complement: Λ ← R[L, B]⁻¹ · R[L, C]; R[L̄, C] ← R[L̄, C] − R[L̄, B] · Λ; R[L, C] ← 0. Arrows: each non-zero Λ[t, c]
applies pivot column t (green) to column c (orange). One 4×4 inversion and one (n×4)(4×4) product do it all at once.
Result (dark gray = updated entries): the pivot rows are zero in C.
column 5 = {3}; column 6 = {3, 7}; column 7 = {7}; column 8 = {1, 6}
Undo the row permutation (implicit index bookkeeping in practice, Lemma 3.2).
Recurse on C = [5, 8].
Node [5, 8]: split into B = [5, 6] (green) and C = [7, 8] (gray). Recurse on B first;
afterwards all pivots found in B are applied to C in one batch.
Leaf 5: column 5 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(5) = 3 is its pivot.
Apply B = [5] to C = [6]: pivot row L = ⟨3⟩. R[3, 6] ≠ 0, so Λ = R[L,B]⁻¹·R[L,C] = 1:
subtract column 5 from column 6 — a Schur complement with k = 1.
Column 6 updated (dark gray): row 3 is now zero to the right of its pivot.
Leaf 6: column 6 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(6) = 7 is its pivot.
Apply B = [5, 6] to C = [7, 8]: pivot rows L = ⟨3, 7⟩ (green), one per column of B.
Permute the rows L to the bottom, in the same order as the columns of B.
After the permutation R[L, B] (orange outline) is lower triangular with non-zero diagonal (Lemma 4.3), hence
invertible in O(k^ω) with k = 2. R[L, C] (dashed) is the block to be zeroed; orange columns are the ones Λ will change.
Schur complement: Λ ← R[L, B]⁻¹ · R[L, C]; R[L̄, C] ← R[L̄, C] − R[L̄, B] · Λ; R[L, C] ← 0. Arrows: each non-zero Λ[t, c]
applies pivot column t (green) to column c (orange). One 2×2 inversion and one (n×2)(2×2) product do it all at once.
Result (dark gray = updated entries): the pivot rows are zero in C.
column 7 = 0; column 8 = {1, 6}
Undo the row permutation (implicit index bookkeeping in practice, Lemma 3.2).
Recurse on C = [7, 8].
Leaf 7: column 7 is zero (orange) — it was reduced by the batch updates of its ancestors.
Swap it with the first unused column of I (column 9, gray). Z ← Z ∪ {7}.
Position 7 now holds e9 with pivot in row 9; the zero column sits at position 9.
Apply B = [7] to C = [8]: pivot row L = ⟨9⟩ (green).
R[L, C] = 0, so Λ = 0 and nothing changes.
Leaf 8: column 8 is non-zero. By the recursion invariant it is already reduced with respect to
all earlier columns (Lemma 4.4), so low(8) = 6 is its pivot.
Done: pivots (5, 1), (2, 2), (8, 3), (4, 4), (3, 5), (7, 6), (6, 8); the columns in Z = {7} were zero and now sit among the identity columns.
Restricted to the first n columns this is the exhaustive reduction (Algorithm 2). Total time O(n^ω), O(n² log n) if ω = 2.

svg.text: if R[·, i] = 0: swap column i with the
next unused column of I; Z ← Z ∪ {i}
B ← left half of A, C ← right half
L ← ⟨low(ℓ) : ℓ ∈ B⟩, permute rows L to the bottom
Λ ← R[L, B]⁻¹ · R[L, C] ▷ k×k inverse
